thread:
anya: RFC follow-up: prefetch architecture choices for telemetry ingest. we prototyped per-shard buffers and a centralized prefetcher. need to pick a path and a safe canary. main tradeoffs: memory vs coord overhead, per-tenant ordering, and earliest possible billing_key emission.

ben: quick take: per-shard buffers are the simplest to reason about (no leader election), but duplicates fetch work and memory grows with active tenants. simple backpressure semantics though.

samir: duplication is the worry. in the PoC a small subset of tenants (the "hot" ones) contributed most memory pressure. we should consider a selective strategy.

lucy: whatever we pick we must guarantee billing_key is present before batching/sending to downstream so cost attribution is immediate. late joins break dashboards. gateway enrichment seems necessary.

tom: shared prefetcher with leasing reduces memory by centralizing buffers. but it needs robust lease handling. leases + rehydrate on fail -> more complex codepaths and CPU for coordination. also more bursty network when leader changes.

anya: proposal: hybrid approach. each shard maintains tiny per-tenant buffers for currently hot tenants; a shared long-tail prefetcher handles the rest. hotness calculated from recent qps. reasons: saves memory while keeping low-latency for heavy tenants.

ben: how do we define hot? and how often do we reevaluate? churn of hot set could cause repeated migration cost.

samir: suggestion: scored hotness using exponential moving average over 30s window, select top-K per shard. add hysteresis windows: only promote/demote if sustained for >45s to avoid thrash.

lucy: billing_key handling: gateway resolves billing_key (tenant_id -> billing_key lookup) and attaches billing_key to the envelope before prefetch. cache in gateway with TTL and watch for explicit metadata invalidation events. prevents prefetch layer needing tenant metadata.

tom: rehydrate: store fetch cursor and buffer snapshot metadata in durable KV (redis/consul) so when leadership moves we can resume without double-emitting. requires idempotent read from source using cursors. ensure cursors are monotonic.

observability-bot: ci: prefetch-hybrid branch tests passed (ci/obs-prefetch #225) :white_check_mark:

anya: telemetry signals to add: prefetch.mode (per-shard/shared/hybrid), prefetch.hot_promotions.count, prefetch.hot_demotions.count, prefetch.migration.duration_ms, prefetch.rehydrate.failures, prefetch.buffer_bytes_per_shard. add trace attributes too.

ben: add alert: if prefetch.migration.rate > 10/min and migration.duration > 2s then page on-call. migrations should be rare and cheap.

samir: fanout tenants: detect if unique_stream_keys > 500 in 1m. route those tenants to dedicated worker pool (dedicated-prefetch class) to avoid saturating shared hot buffers.

lucy: agree. also surface a dashboard slice for big-fanout tenants and a billing export for their extra cost.

anya: config proposal (yaml snippet):
```yaml
prefetch:
  mode: hybrid
  hot_window_sec: 30
  hot_k_per_shard: 150
  hot_promote_hysteresis_sec: 45
  per_tenant_hot_buffer_bytes: 131072 # 128k
  shared_longtail_aggregate_bytes: 2097152 # 2MB
  fanout_threshold_unique_keys: 500
  billing_key_cache_ttl_sec: 300
  migration_grace_ms: 2000
```

ben: that longtail aggregate is a bit larger than PoC but safer for bursts. we can tune downward if CPU/heap is still okay.

samir: rollout plan: 1) implement hybrid + metrics in staging. 2) enable for 1% of traffic (select tenants preferring mid-size and non-prod tenants). 3) monitor memory, migrations, prefetch.latency, billing attribution correctness for 48h. 4) bump to 10% then 25% with stops on alert thresholds.

lucy: tests to add: billing_key attach integration test, migration idempotence test (simulate lease fail), fanout routing e2e.

tom: about durability: KV contract must support compare-and-swap for cursor updates to avoid races. i'll draft that contract.

anya: action items:
- ben: implement gateway billing_key cache + TTL and expose metric for cache hit rate (due Thu)
- tom: durable cursor contract draft + rehydrate sequence (due Wed)
- samir: add migration metrics and alert thresholds to observability dashboards (due Wed)
- lucy: test matrix for billing_key + migration + fanout (due Fri)
- anya: write RFC addendum and canary playbook (due Fri)

ben: one more: consider an admin override to pin specific tenants into hot set or dedicated pool for troubleshooting. useful for customers with performance SLAs.

anya: good idea. we'll add 'pinned_hot_tenants' config and an admin API.
